notes.title: Talents vs Skills in Swords and Sandals Immortals
notes.content:
In this week's behind the scenes from S&S Immortals, I've been working on the Talent Tree system in the game and have decided on some pretty interesting changes that will no doubt add a few weeks of development time. Ultimately I think they will really add to the strategy and customization options of the game.

So, previously in S&S games there have been a few different kinds of talent trees. In S&S 1 and 2 there were no talent trees at all. Instead, you were given a new talent every X levels, be it the ability to Psyche Up at level 10 (or whatever), then maybe the ability to carry 10 items of ammo, and so on.

In S&S 3 (and to an extend in the Redux games) there was a proper RPG talent tree (in fact four, Survival, Arcane, Warfare and Theatrics). You could select from a tree and branch off to different skills and tiers, and most if not all of them were 'passive skills'. At level one you might learn sword mastery to 5 points, axe mastery to another 5 and then once you had ten points in the tree you would gain access to higher tier abilities in that tree.

This is the approach I'm going with for S&S Immortals as I think it allows for lots of variety and specialization.

There will be in fact 6 talent trees to choose from in this game, fitting as its essentially S&S VI after all! The classic Survival, Arcane, Warfare and Theatrics return, as well as two new trees - Adventure ( dealing with skills like haggling, crafting and so on ) and Robotics ( a special tree that is only for Automatons but may be unlocked by non-automatons at some point)

The idea with the Robotics tree is you will potentially be able to replace body parts with mechanical arms and legs and so on, improve your techniques with Automaton weapons etc - this really needs fleshing out but the idea is interesting to me. The Robotics Tree may or may not make the launch date but should happen at some point.

In these attached pictures, you can see a very rough WIP of the Talent Tree selection page ( with no icons for the buttons yet) and a spreadsheet of how I put together talents - it's a Google Doc! Same as items and even text to be translated, I import all these into the game via Google Docs making it quite intuitive and easy to edit, even when I am on a phone away from the computer!

So okay - talents vs skills, what's that all about? I've differentiated the two into "Talents" that you gain when you level up and are entirely passive (such as resistance to fire or extra health). "Skills" will be learned in exchange for gold from the various merchants (and maybe even special NPCS). 

The major reason for this is I don't have to tie skills into the talent trees and limit them to, say 15 spells for the arcane tree). I can have silly little cantrips like "Little Fat Kid" that can shrink your enemy, or powerful skills like "Whirlwind" that can decapitate an enemy.

You will assign these skils to your combat radial wheel (automatically until you fill up the wheel, then you can drag them from your backup skills in your character sheet.) 

Cheers Oli

notes.title: Levelling up in Swords and Sandals Immortals
notes.content:
Gladiators! I've been hard at work on Swords and Sandals Immortals all year but the Steam page has been relatively quiet ... until now. It's time to open the portcullis, step into the Arena and start smoothing the sands for the impending arrival of our gladiators!

Over the coming weeks and months I want to share with you progress updates from the game. These updates were [url=https://www.patreon.com/whiskeybarrelstudios]first posted on my Patreon[/url] a little while ago but it's time to share them with the greater community and get your feedback on what you want to see in the game going forward! Alright, without further ado ...

[h2]The Level Up Screen[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40969784/c75971f7c2010ac393198cbaab3bd7e1257884b8.png[/img]

One of the I've finished up the 'end battle bar' which is quite familiar to those who have played the earlier S&S games. Your gladiator will receive XP and gold based on the enemy's power score.

Once the bar fills, it will turn blue and the next screen you see will be a campfire at night. Some of you may notice the campfire used to be part of the Battle Caravan screen, this has now been moved to its own screen. Someone pointed out to me it looked weird that your little camp was surrounded by all these big tents, so I moved it to its own space - looks a lot less cluttered.

What we will see on this screen is your gladiator asleep by the fire. They suddenly awake, hold up their arm to the sky, a bolt of lightning appear and nice shiny particles will flash as they grow in power!

You will then select a new attribute to increase ( Strength, Agility and so on ), and you'll head to the Talent Tree selection. It actually plays out quite similar to Swords and Sandals III's talent trees. Talents for Warfare, Arcane and Theatrics that you can level up. The key here is to make lots of interesting talents for gladiators to choose from.

There will also be a Robotics talent tree further down the road for Automaton/Cyborg type characters!

In the next update, we'll talk about these talent trees themselves!

Until next time, I salute you!

Oliver Joyce
Whiskeybarrel Studios
